newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 11.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Friday:

* Investors are likely to remain wary of the market on the back of higher interest rates. Although bargain-hunting has commenced, the 2,450 support may still be tested, said Sun Hung Kai Securities in its daily outlook.
* "The fragile situation in the fixed income market continues to provide a caveat to equity investors," said Bernadette Tamayo, analyst at BPI Securities Corp.
* On Thursday, the Philippine composite index hit a two-month closing low settling 78.05 points lower at 2,511.15.
* The Dow Jones on Thursday ended 44.33 points higher at 7,886.76. PLDT's ADR closed up $0/15 at $63.
* The Philippine peso ended slightly lower at 26.401 vs 26.40 to a dollar.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was at 32.15625 percent vs 30.375 percent.
* The Philippines on Thursday raised interest rates again to defend the peso from speculators but appeared helpless to prevent a peso-linked fresh slump in its stock market.
* The Central Bank on Thursday raised overnight lending rate to 34 percent from 32 and overnight borrowing rate to 32 percent from 30 percent.
* The Bank on Thursday lifted its term reverse repo (rrp) rates after raising its overnight rates.

* Pressure on the Philippine peso is reaching a stage when it may make more sense for the government to give in, end the pain, and let its currency slip a litte, analysts and bankers said on Thursday.
* Cebu Holdings Inc said it had approved a two-for-five stock rights offer at a cost of one peso per share.

* First Philippine Holdings Corp said it was postponing its proposed convertible note issue due to adverse market conditions. Earlier, the firm said it planned to issue $300 million worth of Euroconvertible notes.
* The International Container Terminal Services Inc said its group won a bid to manage and operate the container and cargo terminal at King Abdul Aziz sea port in Damman, Saudi Arabia.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange said it decided to suspend a broker accused by a newspaper columnist of using her account without authority.
* Miners exploring for gold in Asia will be undeterred by the sharp price fall of the metal but output from high-cost operators could slow down until values improve, regional industry sources said.

* Manila Bulletin reported that foreign mining firms see that bureaucratic red tape in the issuance of exploration permits may deprive the Philippines of substantial foreign invesments. The paper quoted International Mining and Exploration Committee chairman Malcolm Norris who spoke at the Mining Philippines '97 Conference.
* BusinessWorld said that the Monetary Board, the policy-making arm of the Central is expected to announce major changes in the country's foreign exchange policy today.

Executive Secretary Ruben Torres Thursday night told reporters that the Monetary Board will be asked to refrain from its costly intervention in the currencies market and instead allow the peso to seek its value against the US dollar, the newspaper said.
